notes.meaning: John sees an awesome and startling sign in heaven with seven angels carrying the seven final plagues. These plagues bring God's righteous anger to completion, finishing His judgments against those who rebel against Him. God has shown long patience, but now His holy judgment reaches its final goal.

differ.view: Some evangelicals believe the seals, trumpets, and bowls happen one after another in a straight timeline, while others see them as repeating cycles that describe the same time period with growing intensity.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic commentators note that interpreters differ on whether these plagues were fulfilled in the fall of pagan Rome, unfold across church history, or will occur literally at the end of time.

notes.meaning: John looks across what looks like a clear glass sea mixed with fire, picturing God's holiness combined with fiery judgment. Standing beside this sea are the believers who stayed faithful to God and refused to worship the evil beast or take its mark. They hold harps given by God, showing that peace and joy belong to those who endure fiery trials.

differ.view: The company includes those who had already overcome as well as those who were still in the process of gaining victory, with more yet to join them.

notes.meaning: These victorious believers sing the song of Moses and of the Lamb, joining the praises of the Old and New Testaments into one great hymn. Just as Israel praised God after crossing the Red Sea safely away from Pharaoh, God's people now praise Him for rescuing them from evil. They declare that the Lord God Almighty does wonderful things and that His ways are completely fair and true.

The song asks who could fail to revere the Lord and honor His name, since He alone is completely pure and holy. All nations will come to bow before Him because His fair and just acts have now been shown to the world. True worship comes from seeing that God's judgments are always right.

John looks again and sees the heavenly temple opened, which is called the tent of witness. This is the true dwelling place of God that the earthly tabernacle in the wilderness was patterned after. Opening this sacred room reveals that the coming judgments come straight from God's presence and rest on His holy Law.

The seven angels who carry the plagues come out from the inner sanctuary to do their work. They are dressed in pure, shining linen with gold sashes around their chests, much like priests on holy duty or royal servants on a mission. Their spotless clothing shows that God's coming judgments are completely clean, just, and free from any wrongdoing.

One of the four heavenly living creatures gives seven golden bowls to the seven angels. These wide, shallow bowls resemble dishes used in ancient temple offerings, made to pour out their contents quickly all at once. They are full of the wrath of God, who lives forever, showing that His holy anger against evil cannot be stopped.

The temple fills with thick smoke that displays the glory and mighty power of God. Just as a cloud filled the tabernacle in Moses' day, this smoke shows that God Himself is actively present in judgment. No one can enter the temple while the seven plagues are being poured out, proving that His decree will be carried out to the very end.

differ.view: Some evangelicals teach that no one being able to enter the temple means the time for prayer and mercy has ended, so that judgment is now entirely unavoidable.
